newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE's al-Thuraya lifts capital to $500 mln.
newsitem.headline: UAE's al-Thuraya lifts capital to $500 mln.

text.p: The board of directors of Al-Thurayya, a UAE-based satellite telecommunications company, agreed to increase the company's capital to $500 million from $25 million, the official WAM news agency said on Saturday.

"A memorandum to this effect will be sent to the founding members, telecommunications authorities in the region and to other investment bodies who had expressed a desire to participate in the project," WAM quoted Mohammad Hassan Omran, al-Thurayya's board chairman as saying.
Omran said potential participants in the project will be given one month to respond and indicate the level of their participation.
Al-Thurayya Satellite Telecommunications Company was formed in January to own and operate a new satellite project for mobile communications.
Etisalat, the UAE telecommunications company holds a 26 percent stake in the company and the Arab Satellite Communications Organisation (Arabsat) 10 percent.
Other shareholders include Bahrain Telecommunications Co (10 percent), and Germany's Detcom (0.5 percent).
Officials have said the total cost of the project would be around $800 million.
The al-Thurayya satellite will provide services to UAE users of two-way mobile telephones compatible with the Global System for Mobile Communications (GSM).

The project, due to be operational by the turn of the century, will make services available to remote sea and rural areas and will cover most Arab states, the Indian subcontinent, Central Asia, North Africa and parts of Europe.

Al-Thurayya officials said earlier four telecommunications companies were competing to build the satellite system -- Alcatel and Aerospatiale of France and Hughe's Electronics Corp and Lockheed Martin Corp of the United States.
